objective: Remove Render as a runtime/origin dependency and remove Supabase as an application database dependency without breaking the public storefront, MTG master silo, billboard/avatar surfaces, durable state, authentication boundaries, or Stripe settlement/fulfillment.

target_stack.dynamic_http_runtime: Cloudflare Pages Advanced Mode Worker or Pages Functions, selected only after route-parity and runtime compatibility tests
target_stack.durable_artifacts_if_needed: Cloudflare R2, only after an inventory proves which file-backed artifacts require object storage
target_stack.build_and_release: GitHub Actions with commit-SHA release acceptance
target_stack.domain: Cloudflare DNS, after zone-record inventory and preview acceptance

free_tier_constraints.neon_postgres_network_transfer: VERIFY_CURRENT_ACCOUNT_LIMIT; do not assume 5 GB because Neon’s Oct 2, 2026 update identifies the 5 GB allowance as Object Storage.

cost_policy.capacity_rule: 100,000 requests/day is shared between Workers and Pages Functions and resets at 00:00 UTC. Once a project invokes a Function for a request, request routing must deliberately exclude ordinary static assets if they are to remain unmetered. Treat 10 ms CPU, 50 subrequests and 128 MB memory as hard limits. Measure from day one; 50% usage is observe, 80% requires action, and 90% stops nonessential polling until capacity is reviewed. No paid-plan assumption is part of acceptance. For Neon, track compute hours, maximum compute CU, storage and network transfer separately; include the fixed five-minute idle suspension in first-request latency tests.

authoritative_state_rule: Each gate starts NOT_RUN. PASS requires its named evidence, the exact tested commit SHA, and independent route/persistence checks. Missing credentials, untested behavior, HTTP 200 alone, deploy-hook success, a successful provider control-plane call, or a green static homepage never count as PASS. The final migration stays blocked until every required scoped gate passes.

gates.name: Pin canonical migration branch and source SHA
pass_evidence: repository
branch
base SHA
head SHA
working-tree/diff summary
blocks: All subsequent gates must name the tested commit SHA.

gates.name: Inventory runtime routes and dependencies
pass_evidence: machine-readable route inventory from BEC-PRIME/start.js and all imported preloads/routes
HTTP method and auth classification
per-route dependency list
separate public/static, read-only, stateful, payment, internal and admin classes
blocks: No runtime route may be treated as migrated merely because static HTML exists.

gates.name: Inventory persistent writes and all-schema dependencies before selecting dump scope
pass_evidence: inventory of persistent transaction JSON, revenueLedger JSONL, journals/events/fulfillment, proof files, AgentBridgeEventLedger, DemandRadar, Sentinel, CUBE observations and all Supabase table consumers

all-schema inventory from PostgreSQL catalogs: namespaces, tables, views, materialized views, sequences, enum/domain types, extensions, functions/procedures, triggers, indexes, constraints, grants and dependencies
RLS enabled/forced flags and policies across all application schemas, including any custom policies or triggers attached to auth, storage and realtime objects
custom functions and triggers classified by owning schema and referenced tables/functions; cross-schema dependency graph retained
Supabase-managed internals explicitly separated from application-owned customizations; required replacement behavior specified before choosing target schema scope
Storage buckets and object inventory recorded separately from SQL dump scope, including owner/path/metadata and checksums when readable
scope decision recorded as include, reimplement, replace or exclude with a reason and proof reference before any export/import
blocks: Do not choose a public-only dump or retire source storage until every custom cross-schema dependency, persistent write, read, retention requirement and recovery path is mapped.
Never restore Supabase-managed auth/storage internals blindly into Neon; recreate only application-owned behavior on the target platform.

gates.name: Human provisioning of Cloudflare and Neon free accounts
pass_evidence: Cloudflare account ID and Pages project exist
Neon project and database exist
plan and quota screens recorded without exposing secrets
blocks: Credentials are supplied by the owner through GitHub Actions secrets; do not commit credentials.

gates.name: Provision and verify Neon target schema
pass_evidence: reviewed migration for complete current state model, not only minimal heartbeat schema
schema version recorded
read-only SELECT 1 passes
write/read-back and transaction rollback tests pass on disposable/test records
blocks: NEON-MINIMAL-SCHEMA.sql is a heartbeat/commercial-spine starting schema, not proof that Supabase or file-backed state has been fully migrated.
mutations: Create target schema in the newly provisioned Neon database

gates.name: Map local file-backed ledger to durable database transactions
pass_evidence: transactional tables for payment events, unique event claims, idempotency keys, orders, ledger journals, ledger entries, fulfillment, delivery receipts and evidence
unique constraints for Stripe event IDs, checkout-session/payment IDs, fulfillment identity and deterministic outbox idempotency keys
signed webhook validation followed by one database transaction for durable event claim and all database ledger/order/payment state changes
external fulfillment delivered through a durable outbox with a stable idempotency key recognized by the fulfillment receiver; external effects are never assumed rolled back by a database rollback
duplicate webhook replay, concurrent duplicate delivery, crash/retry and outbox replay tests prove one fulfillment and one ledger effect
a deduplication claim is not deleted after an uncertain failure if any external side effect may already have occurred; reconcile or retry with the same idempotency key
no production route writes authoritative payment, fulfillment or proof state to an ephemeral local filesystem
blocks: Current Node runtime writes revenue journal, fulfillment, transaction and proof files locally. Workers local filesystem is not a durable substitute.

Deleting a deduplication record is safe only if the associated database changes and all associated external side effects are known to have rolled back; external fulfillment requires receiver-side idempotency or reconciliation.

gates.name: Move app database access from Supabase to Neon
pass_evidence: enumeration of every Supabase REST/SQL/Auth/Storage/Realtime/Vault call and every SQL dependency from G02
Neon-compatible repository adapter plus explicit replacement of any required Auth/Storage/Realtime behavior
source data export and row-count/hash manifest scoped by the G02 dependency inventory
import followed by key-by-key or hash-based read-back, with cross-schema dependencies validated
dual-run comparison without duplicated writes, buyer messages or fulfillment
rollback/export proof and retained source backup
blocks: Do not delete/pause the Supabase project before application reads, writes, scheduled jobs and recovery paths are proven independent of it.
mutations: Export/import and controlled test writes against target

gates.name: Implement Cloudflare-compatible request handlers
pass_evidence: Worker/Pages Functions entrypoint independent of Node server.listen()
no dependency on Render environment variables for deployment identity
all required routes individually ported or deliberately disabled with explicit contract
database network access works within the target runtime
CPU, memory, subrequest and payload size tests recorded
static asset requests are excluded from Function invocation by verified _routes.json or an equivalent tested asset routing rule
each deployed handler stays within 10 ms CPU, 50 subrequests and 128 MB memory; 7 ms CPU and 20 subrequests are the internal soft budgets
blocks: Existing BEC-PRIME/start.js wraps node:http.createServer and starts a listener; that server boot is not itself a Cloudflare Worker entrypoint.

gates.name: Public read-only preview acceptance on pages.dev
pass_evidence: same SHA visible at /version
GET / and /mtg/ return expected HTML
GET /healthz returns the documented preview/production status
GET /api/products and /api/offers match current published-only contract
MTG manifest and /data/mtg-catalog.json parse with silo=mtg and currency=NZD
every product with status=published in the deployed MTG catalogue has a detail_url returning 200 HTML with the correct product identity and a working declared claim action
all published MTG catalogue routes are probed from the deployed catalogue itself, including directory-style /buy/ routes; held products are not represented as buyable
root /404.html exists and a unique nonexistent HTML path returns actual HTTP 404 with the not-found document, never the homepage/SPA body
static assets bypass Functions so they do not consume the 100,000/day runtime quota
GET /version SHA is identical to the deployed Git commit SHA
blocks: All results are tied to the preview URL and exact Git SHA. Liveness is not readiness.

gates.name: Stateful route and internal API parity
pass_evidence: Agent Bridge manifest/probe behavior matches contract
internal engine proxy/auth checks pass
all database reads and writes persist after isolate restart
no cross-silo data exposure
timeouts, errors, rate limits and cache policy tested
blocks: Any unported stateful route must remain blocked and the overall production migration remains BLOCKED.

gates.name: Stripe test-mode webhook and checkout acceptance
pass_evidence: test-mode signed webhook verification passes; invalid and stale signatures rejected
a unique durable claim for each Stripe event ID is enforced atomically with database-side order/payment/ledger state changes
duplicate and concurrent event replay return the prior outcome without duplicate entitlement or fulfillment

external fulfillment uses an idempotent durable outbox; failures before an external effect remain retryable, and uncertain outcomes are reconciled without deleting the event claim or creating a second delivery
payment → attribution → ledger → fulfillment → retrievable delivery proof reconciles
event/outbox retry and crash/restart tests pass across process restart
no secret or raw payment payload appears in logs
blocks: Never switch the production Stripe webhook URL until all tests pass. Checkout initiation is not revenue.
mutations: Test-mode Stripe endpoint configuration, if needed

gates.name: Capacity and quota guardrails
pass_evidence: daily Worker invocation budget includes static-vs-function distinction and projected headroom
10 ms CPU p95/p99 measured for all Worker routes
no invocation exceeds 50 subrequests
Neon CU-hours/storage/network tracked
budget threshold emits evidence and blocks unsafe rollout before quota exhaustion
shared Pages Functions plus Workers request counts and UTC reset behavior verified
usage response thresholds are exercised at 50%, 80% and 90%
Neon scale-to-zero wake latency, 100 CU-hours/month, 1 GB Postgres storage and max 2 CU are measured/recorded
current Neon Postgres network-transfer limit checked in the account; 5 GB Object Storage must not be mislabeled as Postgres egress
blocks: Public agent polling and x402 traffic require measured limits; free-tier headroom must not be assumed from today's traffic.
A Pages build quota is not the dynamic runtime quota. Function requests count against the shared Workers free quota.

gates.name: Deploy and prove candidate release identity
pass_evidence: Cloudflare deployment success recorded
deployed /version SHA equals candidate Git SHA
deployment environment and route acceptance result retained
deploy-hook success is not considered acceptance
blocks: No domain cutover unless all required route, persistence and payment gates pass for that same SHA.

gates.name: Pilot custom hostname without changing apex nameservers
pass_evidence: existing MX/TXT/CNAME/A/AAAA records and TTLs captured
www or a dedicated pilot hostname validates on Pages
TLS certificate active
all approved route probes pass on that hostname
email, OAuth callbacks, webhook URLs and canonical URLs reviewed
blocks: Do not change apex NS records during the pilot.

gates.name: Owner-approved DNS cutover
pass_evidence: full current DNS zone export retained
MX/TXT/SPF/DKIM/DMARC and domain-verification records preserved
Cloudflare nameserver delegation verified
apex and www HTTPS probes pass
same-SHA /version and all route tests pass from outside the zone
rollback zone file/old origin documented
blocks: Requires a separate explicit owner approval immediately before mutation. This checklist does not authorize NS changes.

gates.name: Production soak and independent commerce reconciliation
pass_evidence: all routes pass for an owner-chosen soak period
production webhook signature/idempotency and database persistence evidence pass
daily quota and error monitoring works
one real external settlement, correct attribution, fulfillment and delivery proof reconciled before recording revenue
blocks: No revenue claim without independent settlement plus attribution plus fulfillment plus retrievable delivery proof.

gates.name: Remove Render as a dependency
pass_evidence: no production DNS/origin points to Render
no deploy workflow, runtime path, secret or health check requires Render
last successful release and rollback artifacts retained outside Render
Cloudflare route and Neon persistence acceptance remain green
blocks: Do not delete Render before G14 and G15 pass. Deletion itself requires separate explicit owner approval.
mutations: Disable Render deploys and later delete service

gates.name: Remove Supabase application dependency
pass_evidence: application has no Supabase DB/REST/Auth/Storage calls
scheduled jobs and fleet recovery no longer require Supabase
all state has verified Neon/R2 destination and restore proof
retained backup/export is readable and checksummed
blocks: Do not pause or delete Supabase until all services and evidence are independent of it. The initial Neon schema alone is insufficient.
mutations: Disable Supabase use, then separately approve project pause/deletion

database_scope_rule: Never assume public is the complete application schema. First inventory all custom tables, views, sequences, types, functions, triggers, RLS policies, grants, extensions and cross-schema dependencies. Treat Supabase-managed auth/storage/realtime/vault objects separately from customizations that depend on them. Do not copy managed platform internals blindly into Neon; recreate or replace application-owned behaviors explicitly, and inventory Storage object data separately from SQL schema.

preview_execution.failed_gate: Validate account configuration without printing secrets
preview_execution.dispatch_policy: Manual workflow_dispatch only. Automatic branch-push runs are disabled until credentials are configured, avoiding repeated no-secret failures.
preview_execution.next_required_human_action: Add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT in the GitHub repository's protected Actions secrets UI. Do not paste their values into chat or repository files. Then manually run DreamLedger Cloudflare Migration Preview against the migration branch.
